progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: Fresh Year 12 students know plants have stems, roots and leaves. Explain root water uptake and leaf food-making in light before using them to justify independence. Earlier flower route supports only the final contrast.
progression.startsWith: A recognisable strawberry parent is visibly connected to a rooted daughter by a runner stem.
progression.stopsAfter: Explain how roots and leaves develop at a node, why their resource functions support independence, and why the supplied rootless bud does not establish independence. Classification follows the mechanism.
progression.nextLesson: bio-m5-b02b delivery part 3: How bread mould starts growing somewhere new.

teaching.task: Explain how roots and leaves at a runner node allow a strawberry plantlet to become independent.
teaching.causalExplanation: A runner grows from parent stem. At a suitable node, roots and leaves develop. Roots supply water and leaves make food in light, so an established daughter can support growth independently. A rootless earlier bud cannot yet take up its own soil water.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Introduce each term with an object and action in the current picture. Retain only the current causal sentence. Explain before classifying or offering a memory contrast.
teaching.openingDecision: Ask how a connected stem becomes a separate plant. Select actual strawberry structure, not an isolated stem-definition card.
teaching.understandingCheck: An attached bud has leaves but no roots. Students explain whether the supplied state establishes independent growth using the missing resource uptake. Full early model and conditions remain during the separate quiet hold.
teaching.curriculumScope: Focused candidate contribution to B-plants in canonical bio-m5-b02b. Flower and runner are separate delivery parts. Source presence and visual fit do not establish reviewed action coverage.
